🖥 Iran’s Air Force, civil defense body pledge to boost protection of critical infrastructure

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s passive defense organization and the country’s Army Air Force have agreed to expand cooperation to protect critical infrastructure and strengthen defense capabilities, according to a statement by the Army’s public relations department.

Brigadier General Gholamreza Jalali, head of Iran’s Passive Defense Organization, met Air Force Commander Brigadier General Bahman Behmard at the air force headquarters on Sunday to discuss ways of improving coordination and national defense preparedness.
​
Both officials stressed the need to increase the resilience of critical infrastructure, reduce vulnerabilities and enhance the country’s ability to respond to potential threats, drawing on lessons from two recent wars.
​
Jalali said the air force played a strategic role in Iran’s defense posture and its ability to respond rapidly to emerging threats. He described closer cooperation between the two institutions, particularly in protecting vital infrastructure and developing defense capabilities.
​
He said changing threats required updated defense strategies and greater use of the institutions’ combined capabilities to strengthen deterrence.
​
Jalali also highlighted the importance of passive defense in safeguarding essential infrastructure and maintaining deterrence against potential air and missile attacks.
​
Behmard said the air force was ready to expand technical, training and operational cooperation with the passive defense organization.
​
He said experience from recent wars has demonstrated the importance of coordination between the Armed Forces and civilian defense institutions in reducing vulnerabilities and improving response capabilities.
​
The two sides agreed to establish joint specialist working groups to develop practical cooperation programs based on lessons learned from the recent US-Israeli-imposed wars.

📌 Liverpool vs Manchester United preview with predicted lineups, injury updates, team news and head-to-head stats ahead of the Premier League clash at Anfield.

Liverpool host Manchester United at Anfield in a Premier League encounter shaped by contrasting fortunes and a significant change in the visitors' dugout. Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of a United side sitting third from the bottom, while Andoni Iraola's Liverpool occupy fourth place and remain in contention near the top of the table.
​
United arrive with a new manager following Michael Carrick's dismissal, hoping to reverse their worst league start in 40 years. Liverpool, meanwhile, are looking to build on a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace after consecutive defeats, although their recent record against their biggest rivals offers a warning.
​
Both managers have important selection decisions to make, with Liverpool welcoming back several players from injury and Manchester United receiving positive news about key defensive options.

The 54-year-old Argentinian has made a rapid transition from his role with the United States national team, overseeing his final match on Wednesday before preparing for the Anfield fixture.

At his introductory media conference, Pochettino emphasised the importance of restoring confidence rather than dwelling on previous disappointments.

"It is about building our own way here," he said. "The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday."

Captain Bruno Fernandes is expected to play an important role in that process despite speculation surrounding his future and the absence of an agreement over a new contract.

"Bruno is our captain and a very important player, but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top," Pochettino said.
